prompt: The activity of a pure radioactive sample falls from $800\ \text{Bq}$ to $50\ \text{Bq}$ in $20\ \text{h}$. What is the half-life of the nuclide?
markscheme: **C.** $800 \to 50$ is a factor of $16 = 2^4$, so four half-lives pass in $20\ \text{h}$: $T_{1/2} = 5.0\ \text{h}$.

prompt: A nucleus $^{232}_{90}\text{Th}$ emits one alpha particle and then two beta-minus particles. What nucleus is formed?
Which nucleus has the greatest binding energy per nucleon?
markscheme: **C.** Iron-56 lies at the peak of the binding-energy-per-nucleon curve.

prompt: The energy spectrum of beta particles from a nuclide is continuous. This is evidence for
markscheme: **C.** A third particle shares the decay energy, so the beta particle can have a range of energies.

prompt:
A student measures the count rate from a radioactive source. The background count rate is $30\ \text{counts min}^{-1}$.

| $t$ / min | 0 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 40 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Count rate / counts min⁻¹ | 990 | 510 | 270 | 150 | 90 |

**(a)** Determine the half-life of the source, showing your working. **[3]**

**(b)** Suggest why the student measured the background count rate. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Corrected count rates: 960, 480, 240, 120, 60 ✓; the corrected rate halves every 10 min ✓; half-life $= 10$ min ✓

**(b)** The detector records background radiation as well as the source, so it must be subtracted to find the count rate due to the source alone ✓
